content.thinking:
I'm working out the postmortem's facts: the P3 flag toggle at 09:07:17 landed at the same moment as the P2 deploy, and the document names P3 as the trigger. The mechanism looks like a missing guard in average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by the length of bought_this_month and lost its check in revision 383534e, with the flag routing requests into that function.

I'm checking the mechanism against the code and the G5309 log, and it holds, so the cause doesn't rest on an unrun reading. Next I'm laying out the causal chain, starting from the failing account pages, then the ZeroDivisionError, then the P3 flag that routed requests into that function. I'm also checking whether the earlier P1 deploy could be the cause, and the metrics and logs show the service was healthy with P1 in place.

I'm checking whether the earlier P1 deploy could be ruled out, and the baseline metrics and the 08:42–08:54 logs show account pages rendering normally after it. P2 can't be ruled out, since it removed the guard that is part of the mechanism. The flag toggle at P3 is what set it off, so the chain should follow P3.

Now I'm settling the root cause: the revision that removed the empty-month guard went out with P2, and the monthly average divides by a zero count for any shopper with no purchases recorded this month. The P3 flag then routed account page requests into that function, so the cause is the revision and the exposure is the flag. The next step is why so many shoppers have an empty list, which I suspect comes from how the new revision decides "this month" from recorded_at, though I haven't checked that yet.

I'm checking the rollback side next: the flag revert was what stopped the errors, and the deployment platform's outage is what kept the rollback from going through.

I'm weighing whether a nobody-paged finding belongs under contributing factors or under the response, and leaning toward the response, since no on-call person was paged for the alert, with an action item to page them as the fix.

I'm drafting the contributing factors now, starting with the flag: it was switched on for all traffic at 09:07, the same instant the revision with the changed code went out, so there was no gradual ramp that could have limited the failures to a small slice of requests.

I'm drafting the contributing factors and noting that the flag went to all traffic in one step, with no ramp that could have confined the failures to a small share of requests. The process fix is to require flag changes to step up gradually and to stop switching them on at the same moment as the deploy of the code behind them. I'm now checking the test file at the deployed revision for any case covering a shopper with no purchases this month, and I don't see one.

I'm reviewing the contributing factors, and for the missing test case I'm proposing a required check on the spend-summary tests, including the empty-month case, before any change to that module can deploy. I'm dropping the idea of a platform-unavailable factor here, since that belongs under the response rather than before the incident.

Now I'm weighing whether the service could have stayed up with the flag still in place, and I'm checking the response steps: the rollback failed because the deployment platform was unavailable, which goes under what went wrong. The same guard gap is still live on every replica of 383534e, so turning the flag back on would bring the errors back for shoppers with no purchases this month. The action item covering the missed paging is still open.

Now I'm looking at how the action items map onto the fixes: the test check and the flag ramp cover the two contributing factors, and paging on-call goes under detection. I'm also weighing a lock that keeps the monthly-spend flag off until a revision with the empty-month guard is deployed, since the errors would return if it were switched back on.

I'm going through the went-well list now: the onset placement and the change-finding by Argus and the Investigator, the flag revert the Mitigation Agent made once the rollback was blocked, its confirmation of recovery, and the draft fix from the Code-Fix Agent, which I'll name without describing its contents. I'm also noting that Argus moved on to the second candidate cause when the rollback was unavailable.

I'm checking whether the deploy and the flag switch at the same instant actually made the flag revert sufficient, since the faulty path sat behind the flag and the revert didn't need the deployment platform. I'm treating that as a fortunate gating rather than something I can rely on in general. I'm also noting two assumptions: the errors are inferred to come from shoppers with no purchases this month based on the code, not measured per account, and the ClientDisconnected errors before onset look like unrelated background.

I'm pinning down the evidence before the chain: the baseline rate and the normal renders from 08:42 to 08:54 both show the account pages were healthy before onset, so the P1 deploy is cleared. I'm writing the first link of the chain, that shoppers' account page requests started failing with server errors, which I can tie to the spike in the error logs and the typical-rate baseline.

I'm noting that the spend-summary error sits inside average_spend_per_item_this_month, and that requests reached it because the monthly-spend flag was switched on during the onset minute, while the earlier P1 deploy left account pages rendering normally and the error rate at its typical level.

Checking the list of contributing factors and the process fixes against the chain, I'm now comparing the statements about the deploy and the flag timing. The deploy at P2 landed at the same instant as the flag switch, so I'm treating it as not ruled out and as the next link to examine.

I'm settling the root-cause wording now: revision 383534e dropped the guard in average_spend_per_item_this_month that handled a shopper with no purchases this month, so the function divides the month's total by an empty count. The flag routed account-page requests into that path, which is why any such shopper hit the error.

I'm noting that the rollback, the first response step, was blocked because the deployment platform's API server was unavailable, which also cut off restarts and scaling, so that goes under what went wrong. I'm now checking whether anyone was paged for the alert at the time, since the record suggests no on-call person was.

Now I'm noting that the postmortem has to name the paging gap and the rollback failure under what went wrong, not as contributing factors.

action_items.item: Make the spend-summary tests, including a case for a shopper with no purchases this month, a required check that must pass before any change to src/io_shop/spend_summary.py can deploy.

Require flags that route traffic to new code paths, such as monthly-spend-feature, to be ramped up in steps, starting only after the deploy carrying the code has run healthy, rather than switched on for all traffic when the code deploys.
Block monthly-spend-feature from being switched back on until a deployed revision carries the empty-month guard.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call person.
Find out why the deployment platform's API server was unavailable during the incident, and restore a working rollback path for io-shop.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors, and the account page error rate rose well above its usual level.
Account page requests failed because the spend summary raised a division-by-zero error inside average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 65279ee (P1): with it in place, account pages were logged as rendering normally and the account page error rate was at its typical level before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Requests reached that function because feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at P3. Flag evaluations went from all off before the onset, to mostly on during the onset minute, to all on afterwards, and render_spend_summary sends any request with the monthly summary selected to that function. The deploy of revision 383534e at P2 came at the same instant, so the record does not rule it out; the next step covers it.

The flag sent requests into code that could not serve a shopper with no purchases this month: the revision deployed at P2 (read at T10 as running on every replica) had taken out the empty-month guard, so the function divides the month's total by the count of purchases recorded this month with nothing to handle a count of none.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software update took out the protection for shoppers who had bought nothing so far this month, so when a new account-page feature was switched on, the page's monthly spending calculation failed for those shoppers.

contributing_factors.factor: monthly-spend-feature was switched on for all traffic at once, at the same instant the revision carrying the changed code behind it was deployed. Within the onset minute every evaluation was on, and no gradual ramp was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Had the flag been ramped up in small steps after the deploy, only a small share of account-page requests would have reached the failing function before the errors were noticed, which would have limited the harm.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test for a shopper with no purchases this month was seen in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py at the deployed revision. The change that removed the empty-month guard shipped without any seen check catching that the function now fails for that shopper.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test of the empty-month case would have failed against revision 383534e, and the guard's removal could have been caught before the deploy.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

got_lucky: The failing code path sat behind a feature flag that changed at the same moment as the deploy. Reverting the flag, which did not depend on the unreachable deployment platform, was enough to stop the errors.

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the onset in the minute the deploy and the flag switch both landed, which tied the incident to those changes.
Argus moved on to the flag candidate C2 as soon as the rollback for C1 could not be taken, rather than waiting for the deployment platform.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature from ON to OFF. This needed nothing from the deployment platform.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service and judged the flag revert confirmed.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: The first action tried, rolling back the io-shop deployment, could not be taken: the deployment platform's API server was unavailable, which also put restarting, scaling and every other platform action out of reach.
No on-call person was paged for the alert.

input.root_cause: Revision 383534e removed the guard in average_spend_per_item_this_month that handled a shopper with no purchases this month. It also changed the function to decide 'this month' from each purchase's recorded_at. The function now divides the month's total by the number of purchases recorded this month with nothing to handle an empty month, so it raises ZeroDivisionError for any shopper with no purchase recorded this month.
input.still_at_risk: Revision 383534e, which has no empty-month guard, was still running, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would send account-page requests from shoppers with no purchases this month into the same division-by-zero failure.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
